report:
The curve construction and the whole-class comparison argument check out under the displayed product and continuous-potential hypotheses. I cannot certify the entire submission against the exact completion criteria: it leaves general prescribed backgrounds and measures outside this product regime untreated, and the supplied factor notes omit a qualification needed for an essential lower bound.

For the curve argument, truncating the Green kernel gives genuine decreasing κ-psh representatives. Integrability, mean zero and the distributional equation κ+dd^c Q=μ follow from the stated kernel normalization and Fubini. Non-polarity removes the degree-one polar remainder. Bounded corrected-product expansion followed by strict-superlevel restriction establishes the actual finite product N h₀^m⊗μ, including for unbounded Q. Thus the finite equation is established directly, rather than inferred from a subsolution inequality. The separated uniqueness argument correctly compares the full current's mass with its non-pluripolar mass.

The continuous-potential variational proof also survives reconstruction. Rotation smoothing gives finite Dirichlet energy; the absolute-value estimate supplies the H¹-to-L¹(μ) trace. Radial smoothing identifies that trace with genuine canonical restrictions. Jensen proves coercivity, convex lower semicontinuity gives a minimizer, and bounded smooth variations give the exact Euler equation. The Green upper bound then bounds the density relative to μ; uniform kernel tails give boundedness and continuity. Energy tests establish bounded uniqueness and the two barriers. These barriers justify the whole-family O(λ) limit. No smooth-volume density hypothesis enters these steps.

The comparison applications have the required hypotheses. BGL's strict domination principle applies to bounded inputs with a smooth constant strict barrier; BMP is unnecessary. GL2 supplies the equality-set maximum inequality used for max(r_j,p). Because −j<inf p, its first branch lies inside {r>−j}, where the actual truncated measure agrees with the competitor's extended measure. This establishes greatestness against singular competitors without assuming their total mass is finite. The shifted-subsolution argument then establishes a≤c using a fixed finite canonical point and the uniform bound on w_λ. Bounded uniqueness follows; unbounded uniqueness does not, and is correctly withdrawn.

The exponential normalization is correct: subtracting the supremum changes the scalar to c exp(λ sup w_λ). The bounded constructed potentials satisfy the actual E_env stretching definition using constant competitors t inf p. The Frostman tail estimate and weighted-circle example establish substantive singular measures satisfying the kernel condition.

I reconstructed the factor chain conditionally: the quotient and metric computations give volume 24π; normalized quasi-psh compactness supports the Lamari limiting argument; Siu is applied only after a local closed positive correction; the translated-divisor contradiction is valid. The curve-averaging submersion, translation estimate, determinant/root calculation and fixed-δ selection then support the proposed Γ_j construction. Given those Γ_j, Tosatti–Weinkove and AM–GM yield the stated mass-collapse estimate D_j³/V_j².

The unresolved qualification occurs before that last implication. Note n3 asserts p_* = min_{|s|≤1/4}p(s)>0 while referring to an undefined class of 'allowed p from I'. Smoothness, compact support and probability normalization alone do not imply this: a normalized smooth bump supported near s=1/2 has p_*=0, and its displayed limiting matrix vanishes on the proposed inner ζ-region. The supplied text does not specify whether such densities are excluded. Consequently the uniform positive horizontal-block bound, and hence the complete concrete factor dependency as supplied, cannot be certified. An explicit admissibility condition or an explicitly chosen auxiliary density is needed; the asserted positivity is not a task-granted assumption.

There is also a completion-scope limitation. The proposal supplies an intrinsic sufficient test for product measures on product backgrounds, with precise consequences for all three equations. It supplies no criterion or implications for a general fixed (X,h,ν) outside that regime, and expressly retains that problem as open. I have not established a counterexample to the restricted main theorem, so this is not a FAIL verdict.

Harmless citation correction: BT Theorem 2.1 is the decreasing-continuity theorem; the recursive definition is equation (2.1), with multilinearity in Corollary 2.2. Choosing the comparison barrier also ≤0 makes the BGL section conventions explicit. Neither correction changes the argument. Supporting notes and previous reading flags were not treated as granted premises.

passages.statement: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions v₁,…,vₖ on a domain Ω⊂ℂᵈ, k≤d, recursively defined Bedford–Taylor products are positive closed, symmetric and multilinear. If each vᵢ,j decreases pointwise to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic vᵢ, their products converge weakly to the product of the limits. (Bedford–Taylor, 1982, equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.)
passages.quote: where the limit is in the weak topology

passages.statement: For smooth real (1,1) forms θᵢ and bounded genuine quasi-psh φᵢ, smooth-background expansion defines symmetric multilinear products of θᵢ+dd^cφᵢ, independent of decomposition and local in the plurifine topology. These products are non-pluripolar and positive when all input currents are positive. The bounded construction requires no bounded mass property. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, arXiv:2406.01090v1, §2.1 and Proposition 2.1.)
passages.quote: is still local in the plurifine topology.

passages.statement: For a genuine nontrivial psh function v on a complex manifold, its degree-one non-pluripolar current is well-defined and equals 1_{v>−∞}dd^c v. Non-pluripolar products, whenever locally finite, are local in the plurifine topology and satisfy the strict-superlevel truncation identity. (BEGZ, §1.2 and Proposition 1.4.)
passages.quote: Condition (1.2) is always satisfied when p = 1

passages.statement: For a nontrivial subharmonic function on a planar domain, localization to a relatively compact smaller disk gives a harmonic remainder plus the Newton logarithmic potential of a compactly supported finite positive measure, with equality of canonical representatives. (Demailly, I.4.20 and the proof of I.4.21.)

A real distribution on Ω⊂ℂᵈ with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. Decreasing psh limits are psh, and L¹_loc-bounded families of locally integrable psh functions are relatively compact in L¹_loc. (Demailly, I.5.4, I.5.8–5.9.)

A real distribution on Ω⊂ℂᵈ with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. Decreasing psh limits are psh, and L¹_loc-bounded families of locally integrable psh functions are relatively compact in L¹_loc. (Demailly, I.5.4, I.5.8–5.9.)
passages.quote: every bounded subset is relatively compact.

passages.statement: For a smooth semipositive background ω and bounded genuine ω-psh u,v on U, MA_ω(max(u,v))≥1_{u>v}MA_ω(u)+1_{u≤v}MA_ω(v), and the products agree on the strict-superlevel set {u>v}. No positive lower mass or BMP assumption is required. (Guedj–Lu, arXiv:2106.04272, Lemma 1.2.)
passages.quote: Let u, v, ϕ be bounded ω-psh functions in U ⊆ X.

passages.statement: Let X be compact complex, θ smooth real, and ρ≤0 genuine θ-psh with analytic singularities and θ+dd^cρ≥εh for a Hermitian h and ε>0. If genuine θ-psh u,v satisfy ρ≤min(u,v), v≤u+C, and 1_{u<v}MA_θ(u)≤α1_{u<v}MA_θ(v) for 0≤α<1, then u≥v. BMP is not required. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, §4 and Lemma 4.2.)
passages.quote: for some c ∈ [0, 1), then u ≥ v.

passages.statement: On a compact complex n-fold, if a smooth real (1,1) form θ satisfies ∫θ∧Θ≥0 for every smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) form Θ, there is a real distribution u with θ+dd^c u≥0. Closedness of θ is not required. (Lamari, 1999, Lemma 3.3.)
passages.quote: X sera une variété complexe compacte de dimension n

passages.statement: On a compact complex n-fold, if a smooth real (1,1) form θ satisfies ∫θ∧Θ≥0 for every smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) form Θ, there is a real distribution u with θ+dd^c u≥0. Closedness of θ is not required. (Lamari, 1999, Lemma 3.3.)

For a positive closed current T of bidimension (p,p) on a complex manifold and c>0, the geometric Lelong upperlevel set {x:ν(T,x)≥c} is analytic of dimension at most p. Lelong numbers are coordinate invariant and a regular integration-current point has number one. (Demailly, III.5 and III.8.5.)

On a connected compact Hermitian manifold (X,h) of dimension n≥2, every smooth strictly positive volume form Ω admits a scalar c>0 and smooth real u with sup_X u=0, h+dd^c u>0 and (h+dd^c u)^n=cΩ, for dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π). (Tosatti–Weinkove, arXiv:0910.1390v2, Corollary 1, with the corresponding potential rescaling.)
